newsitem.title: INDONESIA: SE Asian Grain - Indonesian corn buying picks-up.
newsitem.headline: SE Asian Grain - Indonesian corn buying picks-up.

text.p: Domestic corn buying is expected to pick up steam in Indonesia following the recent washout of deals with foreign sellers, traders said on Wednesday.

An Indonesian trader said the washouts, amounting to about 70,000 tonnes of U.S. corn contracts, would help trigger local purchases later in the year particularly in Lampung where the harvest is proceeding.
"Some players were starting to buy from Lampung," one trader from the key growing region in South Sumatra said. "I heard they were covering to fulfill their contracts."
The trader quoted Lampung corn at 350-355 rupiah a kg.
"I forsee players turning to the local market for year-end supplies because of the washouts," he said.

Traders, meanwhile, could not confirm a report that Indonesian buyers were in the market for 100,000 tonnes of imported soymeal, but one added that, if true, it could be for January/February delivery.
"It's too late in the year for that amount to arrive by December," the trader said. "It could be for Jan/Feb."
Grain and oilseeds prices around the region remained steady.
Corn was quoted unchanged at 390-400 rupiah a kg in Jakarta from a week ago, with soymeal also holding its ground at 850 rupiah a kg on tight supply.
Thai soymeal prices were mostly steady despite scarce supplies brought about by a slowdown in demand from the pig industry and the impending arrival of imported soymeal, trade sources said.
One vessel, the Wadi Alkamar, is scheduled to arrive at a Thai port between October 12-13 with 36,000 tonnes of Argentine soymeal, they said.
"More are on the way. This lot was imported by end users, so that should promptly help alleviate the shortage," a trader said.
The price of local soymeal was quoted at around 10.45-10.50 baht a kg from 10.45 baht a kg last week.
But demand continued to ease as torrential floods forced pig farmers to sell their livestock to the market over fear the pigs would drown or be killed by water-bourne diseases.
"Lots of young pigs were sold. This had an ill-effect on short-term demand," the trader said.

But industry sources see demand for animal feed rising after the floodwater recedes by early November, as farmers need to raise more pigs to meet strong demand for pork during the Chinese New Year holidays next February.
Teh prices of feed grade corn was quoted firmer at 4.70-4.75 baht a kg compared with 4.60 baht a kg a week ago as floods pinched supplies, trade sources said.
In Malaysia, buyers were generally sidelined for the second straight week, awaiting the release of fresh U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) data on Friday.
The only action was provided by Federal Flour Mills Bhd, which bought 25,000 tonnes of U.S. corn for November shipment and December arrival at around $160 a tonne C&F, traders said.
They said another buyer was seeking 50,000 tonnes of corn for November shipment to trade in Malaysia and was negotiating the price.
"The market price for this is around $155 (a tonne C&F), but it could get lower," a dealer said.
The rest of the trade was quiet, dealers said.
Low-grade wheat, was quoted at 500-550 ringgit a tonne ex-factory/godown central region.
Local soymeal was quoted at 810 ringgit a tonne, while imported soymeal was going for about 805-810 ringgit.
Bulk corn was at 500-550 ringgit ex-factory/godown in the central region.
